:::{#cor-best-predictor-unique}
#### The minimizer of squared-error risk is unique up to probability-1 equality

Let $\Predvar$ and $\Outvar$ be [jointly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-jointly-distributed) random variables with $\E{\Outvar^2} < \infty$.
Every [prediction function](#def-prediction) $\predfnf{\Predvar}$ with $\E{\predfnf{\Predvar}^2} < \infty$
that is a [minimizer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-global-minimizer) of the [squared-error risk](#def-squared-error-risk)
(see @cor-best-predictor-argmin)
satisfies:

$$\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}) = 1$$

:::

::: proof

If $\predfn$ is a [minimizer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-global-minimizer), its [risk](#def-risk) equals that of $\bestpredfn$,
so the equality case of @thm-best-predictor gives $\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-best-predictor-unique}
#### Uniqueness in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor, $\predfn_2\paren{\Predvar} = 4\Predvar$ differs from $\bestpredfnf{\Predvar}$ when $\Predvar = 0$, which has probability $0.5$.
So $\predfn_2$ is not a [minimizer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-global-minimizer), which matches its [risk](#def-risk) $2$ being larger than $1$.

:::
